Khondakar Mahbubuddin Ahmed with Mahbubey Alam- for the petitioner.

parties:
Hajera Bibi ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Noor Jahan Begum & others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
The petitioner Hazera Bibi is a co-sharer of the holdings appertaining to khatian Nos. 165 and 180 of Mouza Majkhandi and Mouza Nazirkha respectively. O.P. No. 3 Abdul Kha Jeque (he was O.P. No. 2 in the pre-emption case) transferred 391/2 sataks of land from both the khatians by registered kabala dated 6.3.72 to O. P. No. 2 Sayed Habibur Rahman (he was O.P. No. 1 in the pre-emption case). By another registered kabala dated the same O.P. No. 3 Abdul Kbaleque transferred another 42 sataks out of Khatian No. 165 to O.P. No.2 Syed Mahibur Rahman. O.P. No. 3 Abdul Khaleque was also a co-sharer of the holdings. O.P. No. 2 Syed Habibur Rahman was a stranger. Ay a kabala dated 26.8.72 O.P No. 2 Syed Habibur Rahman transferred his purchased land hereinafter referred to as the case land to O.P. No. 1 Nurjahan Begum (who was O.P. No. 10 in the pre-emption case). Thereafter on 17.9.73 the petitioner filed an application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-emption of the case land and she deposited the consideration of the two kabalas with statutory compensation. Hazera Bibi owned 5/6 bighas of land. 

 2. The application was contested by opposite party No. 1 Nurjahan Begum contending that since the purchaser Syed Habibur Rahman had already transferred his interest to Nurjahan Begum before filing of the application of pre-emption by the petitioner Hazera Bibi, the petitioner could not maintain the application and was not entitled to get pre-emption. It was further contended that the application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was barred by limitation. 

 10. Petitioner Hazera Bibi deposing as P.W. 1 has stated that she has heard about the disputed kabalas from Kala Mia and Manik Matbar in Sravan after which 4 Sravans passed. She was deposing on 12.5.78 and the reference of Sravan in her evidence corresponds to the Sravan referred to in her petition. P.W. 3 manik Matbar has deposed that she told the petitioner about the kabala in Sravan. He also stated that the purchaser Syed Habibur Rahman never possessed the land and that the seller O.P. No. 2 continued in possession. He further says in cross-execration that when be informed the petitioner Kala Miah was with him. It is, therefore, difficult to agree with the learned trial court that the petitioner Hazera Bibi has failed to adduce any cogent evidence to prove her alleged date of knowledge. It is correct that the petitioner did not give the exact date of her knowledge in her evidence nor could P.W. 3 give the same. The evidence of P.W. 1 that she came to know of the disputed transfers in Sravan from Manik Matbar is corroborated by the evidence of P.W. 3 Manik Matbar who has said that he gave the information to her in Sravan.
